evidence: Parse: environment/assets/seed_data.json (28549 bytes, sha256 a1c65c80...e83740) parses as JSON; solution/app/src/seed_data.json is byte-identical (cmp), and the hash matches the solution/app/src/seed_data.json entry in raw-evidence-index.json. Dockerfile 'COPY assets/ /assets/' ships it. No CSV/TSV assets. Referential integrity (checked with an in-memory Python validator, no files written): 10 users/3 jobs/16 applications with unique ids and unique emails; every job.recruiter_id is a recruiter and every manager_id a hiring_manager; interview_limit integers 3/2/3 within 1..50 (rules s.2); every application.job_id resolves; stage values all in the stages list; no duplicate (job, lowercased email); every candidate_email that matches a candidate account carries the same name (Noor Haddad on APP-101 and APP-302, Tomas Varga APP-201, Lena Fischer APP-301); positions are contiguous 1..n per (job, stage) (e.g. JOB-PLAT APPLIED 1,2,3 = Greta Lindqvist, Ade Bello, Marco Rossi; SCREEN 1,2 = Priya Nair, Samuel Ortiz, matching functional protocol Z); Interview occupancy 2/3, 1/2, 1/3 does not exceed limits; the only REJECTED card (APP-301) has rejected_from SCREEN (a non-Hired stage) and a non-blank reason, and no other card carries rejected_from/reject_reason. All 127 messages resolve application_id and sender_id; every sender is a legitimate participant under rules s.6 (recruiters anywhere, candidates only in their own thread, no observer or wrong-job manager senders); no blank bodies; per-thread timestamps strictly increasing (APP-101 120 messages 2026-07-01..07-16, so it exceeds thread_page_size 30 as rules s.9 'one conversation is long' says). All 3 notes resolve and their authors may write there (USR-MGR1 on JOB-PLAT, USR-REC1, USR-MGR3 on JOB-DSGN). All 6 read markers resolve to a participant of that conversation with 0 < read_count <= thread length; computed unread under rules s.6 gives Lena (USR-CAN3) 1 on APP-301, matching functional prompt Z ('the starting read markers give her 1'), and the seeded note text matches Z's quoted 'Strong systems answers; weaker on incident follow-up.'. stages and candidate_status_labels match the rules s.3/s.7 table; thread_page_size 30 matches s.6. Synthetic/clean: every email is on reserved .example domains (hireops.example, candidates.example, mail.example; regex for any other domain found none); names are ordinary invented names with no DOB, phone (regex found none), address or ID numbers; no non-ASCII, '<', '>', 'javascript:', template markers, SQL keywords, 'ignore previous' style prompt-injection text, or the words password/secret/token/api key anywhere in the seed. The demo password Hireops!2026 lives only in instruction.md and hireops_rules.md, which the skill and internal annotation treat as expected, not in the seed data. The golden loader (solution/app/src/db.js:61-84) consumes every seed collection, maps read_count to a message id and seeds once. Adversarial: a broken app that copies the seed into a static page cannot use the seed to pre-satisfy anything here (probe values are review-suffixed per functional prompt line 15); a naive unread implementation (thread length minus read_count) would show USR-REC3 1 on APP-301 and USR-CAN1 1 on APP-101, which is wrong under the public rule 'A person's own messages are never unread for them', so the seed discriminates rather than misleads. A conforming alternative (marker stored as count or as message id, own messages excluded) yields the same counts as the golden, so the seed does not penalise it. Note (not a defect): two markers sit below the reader's own latest message (USR-CAN1 119 while sending #120 on APP-101; USR-REC3 2 while sending #3 on APP-301), a state that 'sending counts as having read' would not produce live; it has no observable effect under the public unread and seen rules (unread 0 either way; seen depends only on the other party's marker). Minor narrative quirk: APP-301 recruiter message 'We will write again once the panel has met' on a card rejected from Screen; move times are not seeded, so it is not a contradiction. Static row: fully verifiable from source bytes; no runtime evidence is required for it, and none is claimed.
